title: OpenAI on Securing Code-Executing AI Agents — Fouad Matin (Codex, Agent Robustness)
talk_summary: Fouad Matin (OpenAI Codex) argues that code-executing agents need system-level guardrails, not just model-level ones: sandbox each agent in its own container/OS sandbox, restrict network egress via allowlists, and keep humans reviewing final diffs. He stresses that LLM-based monitors and PR reviewers are useful but not a substitute for deterministic controls.

takeaways.technique: Per-agent isolated sandbox with PR-only output
takeaways.what_they_do: Run each code-executing agent in its own container/VM that is fully isolated, and have it emit a PR at the end rather than touching shared state.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the best method is just to give it its own computer... It spins up a container fully isolated. It then produces a PR at the end

takeaways.what_they_do: Disable internet by default in the sandbox; when access is needed, expose a configurable allowlist of domains/HTTP methods so prompt-injected content can't exfiltrate code or secrets.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can now turn on internet access but it comes with a set of configurable allow list

takeaways.what_they_do: Treat LLM PR reviewers/monitors as helpful but insufficient; rely on deterministic system controls and human review of the final diff for the authoritative gate.
takeaways.evidence_quote: using LMS as part of that loop, while useful, is not a substitute for a human actually going in and reviewing

takeaways.what_they_do: Expose a dependency-vulnerability service (Socket) as an MCP tool so the agent verifies a package before installing it, plus a post-rollout system check on installed deps.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can expose that to the agent to then go in and verify whether or not a given dependency it's about to install could be vulnerable or suspicious

takeaways.technique: Let the model drive tool/code choice instead of hardcoded loops
takeaways.what_they_do: Replace multi-stage prompt-routing/chaining pipelines with a single reasoning model that decides when to write and run code and which tools to call.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You can actually just have the model decide when it should use which tools and when it should write or run code

takeaways.what_they_do: Offer a 'full auto' sandbox mode (read/write only in cwd, network only for pre-approved commands) as the middle ground between approving every command and no guardrails.
